24:2When Saul returned from following the foreigners, it was reported to him that David was in the wilderness of En-gedi.
24:3He took with him three thousand chosen men from all Israel and went to seek David and his men in front of Sadaiem.
24:4He came to the flocks’ herds beside the road, and there was a cave there. Saul entered to attend to himself. David and his men were sitting farther inside the cave.

24:5David’s men said to him, “Behold, this is the day of which the Lord spoke to you, to hand your enemy into your hands, and you shall do to him as is good in your eyes.” David rose and secretly removed the flap of Saul’s double cloak.
24:6After these things David’s heart struck him because he had removed the flap of his double cloak.
24:7David said to his men, “May the Lord forbid that I should do this to my lord, the Lord’s anointed, by bringing my hand against him, for this one is the Lord’s anointed.”
24:8David persuaded his men with words and did not let them rise and put Saul to death. Saul rose and went down to the road.
24:9David rose behind him from the cave, and David called after Saul, saying, “Lord king!” Saul looked behind him, and David bent with his face to the ground and bowed to him.
24:10David said to Saul, “Why do you listen to the people’s words, saying, ‘Behold, David seeks your soul’?

24:11Behold, on this day your eyes have seen how the Lord handed you into my hand today in the cave. I was unwilling to kill you and spared you. I said, ‘I will not bring my hand against my lord, for this one is the Lord’s anointed.’

24:12Behold, the flap of your double cloak is in my hand! I removed the flap and did not kill you. Know and see today that there is no evil in my hand, nor impiety or rejection. I have not sinned against you, yet you bind my soul to take it.
24:13May the Lord judge between me and you, and may the Lord avenge me on you, but my hand shall not be against you.
24:14As the ancient proverb says, ‘From the lawless comes wrongdoing,’ but my hand shall not be against you.
24:15Now, after whom are you coming out, O king of Israel? Whom are you pursuing? After a dead dog and after a single flea!
24:16May the Lord be judge and arbiter between me and you. May the Lord see, judge my case, and give judgment for me from your hand.”
24:17When David finished speaking these words to Saul, Saul said, “Is this your voice, child David?” Saul raised his voice and wept.
24:18Saul said to David, “You are more righteous than I, for you have repaid me with good things, but I have repaid you with evil things.
24:19Today you have reported to me the good things you did to me, how the Lord shut me into your hands today and you did not kill me.
24:20If someone finds his enemy in distress and sends him away on a good road, the Lord will repay him with good things, as you have done today.
24:21Now behold, I know that you shall surely reign, and Israel’s kingdom shall be established in your hands.
24:22Now swear to me by the Lord that you will not destroy my seed after me or make my name disappear from my father’s house.”
24:23David swore to Saul. Saul went to his place, and David and his men went up to narrow Messara.
25:1Samuel died. All Israel gathered, mourned him, and buried him at his house in Armathaim. David rose and went down to the wilderness of Maan.
25:2A man lived in Maan, with his flocks at Carmel. The man was very great: he had three thousand sheep and a thousand goats. He was shearing his flock at Carmel.

25:3The man’s name was Nabal, and his wife’s name was Abigail. His wife had good understanding and was very beautiful in appearance, but the man was harsh and evil in his practices. The man was doglike.
25:4David heard in the wilderness that Nabal the Carmelite was shearing his flock.
25:5David sent ten young men and said to the young men, “Go up to Carmel, go to Nabal, and ask about his welfare in my name.
25:6Say this: ‘To the seasons! May it be well with you, and may your house and all that is yours be well.
25:7Now behold, I have heard that they are shearing for you. Your shepherds were with us in the wilderness; we did not hinder them or impose any order on them all the days they were at Carmel.
25:8Ask your young men, and they will tell you. Let the young men find favour in your eyes, for we have come on a good day. Please give whatever your hand finds to your son David.’”
25:9The young men came and spoke these words to Nabal, according to all these sayings, in David’s name. Then he sprang up,
25:10and Nabal answered David’s servants and said, “Who is David, and who is Jesse’s son? Today many slaves withdraw, each from his master.
25:11Shall I take my loaves, my wine, and my slaughtered offerings—the sheep I slaughtered for my shearers—and give them to men whose origin I do not know?”
25:12David’s young men turned onto their way, returned, came, and reported to David according to these words.
25:13David said to his men, “Each of you strap on his sword.” About four hundred men went up after David, while the two hundred stayed with the equipment.
25:14One of the young men reported to Abigail, Nabal’s wife, saying, “Behold, David sent messengers from the wilderness to bless our master, and he turned away from them.
25:15The men were very good to us. They did not hinder us or impose orders on us all the days we were with them. While we were in the field,
25:16they were like a wall around us by night and by day, all the days we were with them tending the flock.
25:17Now know and see what you will do, for evil has been determined against our master and his house. He is a pestilent son, and one cannot speak to him.”
25:18Abigail hurried and took two hundred loaves, two vessels of wine, five prepared sheep, five oiphi of barley meal, one gomor of raisins, and two hundred fig cakes. She placed them on the donkeys.
25:19She said to her young men, “Go on before me. Behold, I am coming after you.” She did not tell her husband.
25:20As she rode on the donkey and came down under cover of the mountain, there were David and his men coming down to meet her. She met them.
25:21David said, “Perhaps it was for an unjust man that I guarded all his possessions in the wilderness. We imposed no order to take anything of all he had, yet he has repaid me evil for good.
25:22May God do so to David, and more besides, if I leave by morning anyone of all Nabal has who urinates against a wall.”
25:23Abigail saw David, hurried, and jumped down from the donkey. She fell before David on her face and bowed to him on the ground,
25:24at his feet, and said, “On me, my lord, be the wrong. Please let your handmaid speak in your ears, and hear your handmaid’s word.

25:25Please let my lord not set his heart on this pestilent man, for as his name is, so is he: Nabal is his name, and folly is with him. But I, your handmaid, did not see your young men whom you sent.

25:26Now, lord, as the Lord lives and as your soul lives, the Lord has restrained you from coming into innocent blood and from saving your hand for yourself. Now may your enemies and those seeking evil for my lord become like Nabal.
25:27Now take this blessing, which your handmaid has brought to my lord, and give it to the young men who stand beside my lord.
25:28Please take away your handmaid’s lawless deed. The Lord will surely make my lord a faithful house, for my lord fights the Lord’s war, and evil shall never be found in you.

25:29A person will rise to pursue you and seek your soul, but my lord’s soul shall be bound in the bond of life beside the Lord God. You shall sling the soul of your enemies in the midst of the sling.
25:30When the Lord does for my lord all the good things He has spoken concerning you, and the Lord appoints you leader over Israel,

25:31this shall not be an abomination or a stumbling block for my lord: pouring out innocent blood without cause and saving my lord’s hand for himself. The Lord will do good to my lord, and you shall remember your handmaid to do good to her.”
25:32David said to Abigail, “Blessed be the Lord, the God of Israel, who sent you today, on this day, to meet me.
25:33Blessed be your manner, and blessed are you, who kept me today, on this day, from coming into bloodguilt and from saving my hand for myself.

25:34But as the Lord the God of Israel lives, who restrained me today from harming you, if you had not hurried and come to meet me—then I said: ‘No one belonging to Nabal who urinates against a wall shall remain by morning light.’”
25:35David took from her hand all that she had brought him and said to her, “Go up in peace to your house. See, I have listened to your voice and favoured your face.”

25:36Abigail came to Nabal, and there he was holding a drinking feast in his house like a king’s drinking feast. Nabal’s heart was merry within him, and he was very drunk. She told him nothing, small or great, until morning light.
25:37In the morning, when Nabal had sobered from the wine, his wife told him these things. His heart died within him, and he became like stone.
25:38About ten days later the Lord struck Nabal, and he died.

25:39David heard and said, “Blessed be the Lord, who has judged the case of my reproach from Nabal’s hand and preserved His servant from the hand of evil things. The Lord has returned Nabal’s evil on his own head.” David sent and spoke concerning Abigail, to take her as his wife.
25:40David’s servants came to Abigail at Carmel and spoke to her, saying, “David has sent us to you to take you as his wife.”
25:41She rose, bowed to the ground on her face, and said, “Here is your handmaid, a maid to wash the feet of your servants.”
25:42Abigail rose and mounted the donkey, and five girls followed her. She went after David’s servants and became his wife.
25:43David took Ahinoam from Jezreel, and both were his wives.
25:44Saul gave his daughter Michal, David’s wife, to Palti son of Laish, who was from Romma.
26:1The Ziphites came from the parched land to Saul on the hill, saying, “Behold, David is sheltering among us on the hill of Echela, opposite Jessaimoun.”
26:2Saul rose and went down to the wilderness of Ziph, with three thousand chosen men from Israel, to seek David in the wilderness of Ziph.
26:3Saul camped on the hill of Echela, opposite Jessaimoun, beside the road. David stayed in the wilderness. David saw that Saul had come after him into the wilderness.
26:4David sent spies and knew that Saul had come prepared from Keilah.
26:5David rose secretly and entered the place where Saul slept, with Abner son of Ner, his chief commander, there. Saul slept in a covered carriage, and the people camped around him.
26:6David answered and said to Ahimelech the Hittite and Abishai son of Zeruiah, Joab’s brother, “Who will enter with me to Saul in the camp?” Abishai said, “I will enter with you.”
26:7David and Abishai entered among the people by night. There was Saul, lying asleep in the covered carriage, the spear fixed in the ground at his head. Abner and his people slept around him.
26:8Abishai said to David, “The Lord has shut your enemy into your hands today. Now I will strike him with the spear to the ground once; I will not strike him a second time.”
26:9David said to Abishai, “Do not humble him. Who will bring his hand against the Lord’s anointed and be acquitted?”
26:10David said, “As the Lord lives, surely the Lord will strike him, or his day will come and he will die, or he will go down into war and be added.
26:11May the Lord forbid that I should bring my hand against the Lord’s anointed. Now please take the spear from beside his head and the water flask, and let us go by ourselves.”

26:12David took the spear and water flask from beside his head, and they went away by themselves. No one saw, no one knew, and no one awoke; all were sleeping, because a stupor from the Lord had fallen upon them.
26:13David crossed to the other side and stood far away on the mountain’s summit, with a long way between them.
26:14David called the people and spoke to Abner, saying, “Will you not answer, Abner?” Abner answered, “Who are you, calling me?”
26:15David said to Abner, “Are you not a man? Who is like you in Israel? Why do you not guard your lord the king? One of the people entered to destroy the king, your lord.

26:16This thing you have done is not good. As the Lord lives, you are sons of execution, you who guard the king, your lord, the Lord’s anointed. Now look: the king’s spear and the water flask—where are the things that were at his head?”
26:17Saul recognized David’s voice and said, “Is this your voice, child David?” David said, “Your servant, lord king.”
26:18He said, “Why does my lord pursue his servant in this way? How have I sinned, and what wrong has been found in me?

26:19Now please let my lord the king hear his servant’s word. If God is stirring you up against me, may He smell your sacrifice. But if human beings have done so, cursed are they before the Lord, for they have expelled me today from being established in the Lord’s inheritance, saying, ‘Go, serve other gods.’
26:20Now let my blood not fall to the ground opposite the Lord’s presence. Israel’s king has come out to seek my soul, as the night-raven pursues in the mountains.”
26:21Saul said, “I have sinned. Return, child David, for I will not harm you, because my soul was honoured in your eyes today. I have acted vainly and been very ignorant.”
26:22David answered, “Here is the king’s spear. Let one of the young men come across and take it.
26:23The Lord will repay each his righteous deeds and faithfulness, for the Lord handed you into my hands today, but I was unwilling to bring my hand against the Lord’s anointed.
26:24Behold, as your soul was magnified in my eyes today, on this day, so may my soul be magnified before the Lord. May He shelter me, and He will rescue me from every affliction.”
26:25Saul said to David, “Blessed are you, child. You shall surely accomplish, and you shall surely be able.” David went on his way, and Saul returned to his place.

27:1David said in his heart, “Now I shall be added one day into Saul’s hands. There is no good for me unless I escape to the foreigners’ land and Saul gives up seeking me throughout Israel’s territory. I shall escape from his hand.”
27:2David and the four hundred men with him rose and went to Achish son of Ammach, king of Gath.
27:3David stayed with Achish at Gath, he and his men, each with his household; David with both his wives, Ahinoam the Jezreelite and Abigail, the wife of Nabal the Carmelite.
27:4It was reported to Saul that David had fled to Gath, and he no longer sought him.

27:5David said to Achish, “If your servant has found favour in your eyes, please let them give me a place in one of the country towns, and I will stay there. Why should your servant stay with you in a royal city?”
27:6He gave him Ziklag that day. Therefore Ziklag has belonged to the king of Judea to this day.
27:7The number of days David stayed in the foreigners’ country was four months.
27:8David and his men went up and attacked all the Gesiri and the Amalekite. Behold, the land—from Gelampsour as far as the land of Egypt—was inhabited with suitable fortified settlements.
27:9He struck the land and left neither man nor woman alive. He took flocks, herds, donkeys, camels, and clothing, and they returned and came to Achish.
27:10Achish said to David, “Whom have you attacked today?” David said to Achish, “The south of Judea, the south of Jesmega, and the south of Kenezi.”

27:11He left neither man nor woman alive to bring to Gath, saying, “Let them not report to Gath against us, saying, ‘This is what David does.’” This was his established practice all the days David stayed in the foreigners’ country.
27:12David was greatly trusted by Achish, who said, “He has made himself utterly shamed among his people Israel, and he will be my slave for ever.”
28:1In those days the foreigners gathered in their camps to go out and fight with Israel. Achish said to David, “Know for certain that you will go out with me to war, you and your men.”
28:2David said to Achish, “So now you will know what your servant will do.” Achish said to David, “So I will make you chief bodyguard all the days.”
28:3Samuel had died, and all Israel had mourned him and buried him at Armathaim, in his city. Saul had removed the mediums and the knowers from the land.
28:4The foreigners gathered, came, and camped at Soman. Saul gathered every man of Israel, and they camped at Gilboa.
28:5Saul saw the foreigners’ camp and was afraid, and his heart was greatly astounded.
28:6Saul inquired through the Lord, but the Lord did not answer him by dreams, by clear signs, or by prophets.
28:7Saul said to his servants, “Find me a woman who is a medium, so that I may go to her and inquire through her.” His servants said to him, “There is a woman who is a medium at Endor.”

28:8Saul concealed himself, put on other garments, and went, with two men beside him. They came to the woman by night. He said to her, “Please divine for me through the medium and bring up for me the one I name to you.”
28:9The woman said to him, “Behold, you know what Saul has done, how he destroyed the mediums and the knowers from the land. Why are you laying a snare for my soul, to put it to death?”
28:10Saul swore to her, saying, “As the Lord lives, no wrong shall come upon you in this matter.”
28:11The woman said, “Whom shall I bring up for you?” He said, “Bring up Samuel for me.”
28:12The woman saw Samuel and cried out with a loud voice. The woman said to Saul, “Why have you deceived me? You are Saul!”
28:13The king said to her, “Do not fear. Tell me whom you have seen.” She said to him, “I have seen gods coming up from the earth.”

28:14He said to her, “What did you perceive?” She said to him, “A man standing upright is coming up from the earth, wrapped in a double cloak.” Saul knew that this was Samuel, and he bent with his face to the ground and bowed to him.

28:15Samuel said, “Why have you troubled me, that I should come up?” Saul said, “I am greatly afflicted. The foreigners are fighting against me, and God has departed from me and no longer listens to me, either through the prophets or by dreams. Now I have called you to make known to me what I should do.”
28:16Samuel said, “Why do you inquire of me, when the Lord has departed from you and has come to be with your neighbour?
28:17The Lord has done to you as He spoke by my hand. The Lord will tear your kingdom from your hand and give it to your neighbour David.
28:18Because you did not listen to the Lord’s voice and did not carry out His furious anger against Amalek, the Lord has done this thing to you this day.
28:19The Lord will hand Israel with you into the foreigners’ hands. Tomorrow you and your sons with you will fall. The Lord will give Israel’s camp into the foreigners’ hands.”

28:20Saul hurried and fell from his standing position to the ground. He was greatly afraid because of Samuel’s words. No strength remained in him, for he had eaten no bread all the day and all that night.
28:21The woman came in to Saul and saw that he had hurried greatly. She said to him, “Behold, your handmaid listened to your voice. I put my soul in my hand and listened to the words you spoke to me.
28:22Now please listen to your handmaid’s voice. I will set a morsel of bread before you. Eat, and you will have strength, for you will go on your way.”
28:23He was unwilling to eat. His servants and the woman urged him, and he listened to their voice. He rose from the ground and sat on the seat.
28:24The woman had a grazing heifer in the house. She hurried and slaughtered it, took flour, kneaded it, and baked unleavened cakes.
28:25She brought the food before Saul and his servants, and they ate. They rose and went away that night.
29:1The foreigners gathered all their camps at Aphek, and Israel camped at Aendor in Jezreel.
29:2The foreigners’ satraps were passing by in hundreds and thousands, and David and his men were passing by at the rear with Achish.

29:3The foreigners’ satraps said, “Who are these men passing through?” Achish said to the foreigners’ generals, “Is this not David, the servant of Saul king of Israel? He has been with us for days, this being the second year, and I have found nothing against him from the day he came over to me until this day.”

29:4The foreigners’ generals were distressed with him and said to him, “Send the man back to his place, where you stationed him. He must not come with us into the war or become a plotter against the camp. With what could this man be reconciled to his master? Would it not be with the heads of those men?
29:5Is this not David, for whom they led the song in the dances, saying: ‘Saul has struck down his thousands, and David his tens of thousands’?”

29:6Achish called David and said to him, “As the Lord lives, you are upright and good in my eyes, as are your going out and coming in with me in the camp. I have found no evil against you from the day you came to me until today. But in the satraps’ eyes you are not good.
29:7Now return and go in peace, and you shall certainly do no evil in the eyes of the foreigners’ satraps.”

29:8David said to Achish, “What have I done to you? What have you found in your servant, from the day I was before you until this day, that I should certainly not come to fight the enemies of my lord the king?”
29:9Achish answered David, “I know that you are good in my eyes, but the foreigners’ satraps say, ‘He will not come with us into war.’

29:10Now rise early in the morning, you and your master’s servants who came with you. Go to the place where I stationed you. Put no pestilent thought in your heart, for you are good before me. Rise early for the journey; let there be light for you, and go.”
29:11David rose early, he and his men, to leave and guard the land of the foreigners. The foreigners went up to wage war against Israel.
30:1When David and his men entered Ziklag on the third day, Amalek had attacked the south and Ziklag, struck Ziklag, and burned it with fire.
30:2The women and everything in it, from small to great—they killed neither man nor woman, but took them captive and went on their way.
30:3David and his men came to the city, and there it was, burned with fire. Their wives, sons and daughters had been taken captive.
30:4David and his men raised their voices and wept until they no longer had strength to weep.
30:5Both David’s wives had been taken captive: Ahinoam the Jezreelite and Abigail, the wife of Nabal the Carmelite.
30:6David was greatly afflicted, for the people spoke of stoning him. The soul of all the people was in anguish, each over his sons and daughters. But David was strengthened in the Lord his God.
30:7David said to Abiathar the priest, son of Ahimelech, “Bring the ephoud.”
30:8David inquired through the Lord, “Shall I pursue this geddour? Will I overtake them?” He said to him, “Pursue, for you will certainly overtake and certainly rescue.”
30:9David went, he and the six hundred men with him. They came to the Bosor torrent, and those remaining stood still.
30:10He pursued with four hundred men. Two hundred men stayed behind, who sat beyond the Bosor torrent.
30:11They found an Egyptian man in a field, took him, and brought him to David in a field. They gave him bread, and he ate; they gave him water to drink.
30:12They gave him a piece of fruit cake, and he ate. His spirit settled within him, for he had eaten no bread and drunk no water for three days and three nights.
30:13David said to him, “To whom do you belong, and where are you from?” The Egyptian youth said, “I am a slave of an Amalekite man. My master left me because I fell ill; today is the third day.
30:14We attacked the south of Cholthi, the regions of Judea, and the south of Cheloub. We burned Ziklag with fire.”

30:15David said to him, “Will you take me down to this geddour?” He said, “Please swear to me by God that you will neither put me to death nor hand me over into my master’s hands, and I will take you down to this geddour.”

30:16He took him down there, and there they were, scattered over the whole land, eating, drinking and celebrating with all the great spoils they had taken from the land of the foreigners and the land of Judah.
30:17David came upon them and struck them from daybreak until evening, and on the following day. No man among them was saved except four hundred youths who had mounted camels and fled.
30:18David recovered everything the Amalekites had taken, and he rescued both his wives.
30:19Nothing belonging to them was missing, from small to great, from the spoils to sons and daughters and everything they had taken from them. David brought it all back.
30:20David took all the flocks and herds and led them ahead of the spoils. Concerning those spoils it was said, “These are David’s spoils.”

30:21David came to the two hundred men who had grown too weak to follow David and whom he had seated at the Bosor torrent. They came out to meet David and the people with him. David approached the people, and they asked him about his welfare.

30:22Every pestilent and evil man among the warriors who had gone with David answered. They said, “Because they did not pursue with us, we will give them none of the spoils we rescued. Let each take only his wife and children and return.”
30:23David said, “You must not do this, after the Lord has given to us and guarded us. The Lord delivered into our hands the geddour that came against us.

30:24Who would listen to these words of yours? For they are no less than you. As is the share of the one who goes down into war, so shall be the share of the one who stays with the equipment. They shall share equally.”
30:25From that day onward, it became a command and a rule for Israel, until today.
30:26David came to Ziklag and sent some of the spoils to the elders of Judah and to his neighbors, saying, “Behold, from the spoils of the Lord’s enemies.”
30:27He sent it to those in Beth-zur, Ramah of the south and Jeththor;
30:28to those in Aroer, to the Ammadi, and to those in Saphi and Esthie;
30:28ato those in Gath, Kinan, Saphek and Thimath;
30:29to those in Carmel, the cities of the Ierameli, and the cities of the Kenezi;
30:30to those in Ierimouth, Beer-sheba and Noo;
30:31to those in Hebron, and to all the places through which David and his men had passed.
31:1The foreigners were fighting against Israel. The men of Israel fled before the foreigners and fell wounded on Mount Gelboue.
31:2The foreigners closed in on Saul and his sons. The foreigners struck down Jonathan, Aminadab and Melchisa, Saul’s sons.
31:3The war grew heavy against Saul. The missile-throwers, men who were archers, found him, and he was wounded beneath the ribs.

31:4Saul said to his armour-bearer, “Draw your sword and pierce me with it, lest these uncircumcised men come, pierce me, and mock me.” His armour-bearer was unwilling, for he was greatly afraid. Saul took the sword and fell on it.
31:5His armour-bearer saw that Saul was dead. He too fell on his sword and died with him.
31:6Saul died, and his three sons and his armour-bearer, together on that day.

31:7The men of Israel beyond the valley and beyond the Jordan saw that the men of Israel had fled and that Saul and his sons had died. They abandoned their cities and fled. The foreigners came and lived in them.
31:8On the following day, the foreigners came to strip the dead. They found Saul and his three sons fallen on the mountains of Gelboue.
31:9They turned him over and stripped off his equipment. They sent it throughout the surrounding land of the foreigners, announcing the news to their idols and their people.
31:10They dedicated his equipment in the temple of Astarte and fastened his body to the wall of Beth-shan.
31:11The inhabitants of Jabesh in Gilead heard what the foreigners had done to Saul.
31:12All the mighty men rose and traveled the whole night. They took Saul’s body and the body of Jonathan his son from the wall of Beth-shan, brought them to Jabesh, and burned them there.
31:13They took their bones and buried them beneath the cultivated ground at Jabesh. They fasted seven days.
